head: pr17396-r13
report:
Now turn-recovery: the hold logic.

I found no defects in this change. Every earlier finding is either closed at this head or was an open item the author had already disclosed.

NO DEFECTS

## NOT A DEFECT

**What changed since the last round.** Header retry waits are no longer read back out of the error text. Every provider that calls `AIError.finalize` now sets them as a separate field, `AssistantMessage.errorRetryAfterMs`. The consumers that use that field are turn recovery (the usage-limit mark, the retry delay, and `limits.rotate` via a new `retryAfterMs` option), the advisor retry path, the one-shot retry, the auth gateway and `RateLimits.rotate`. `providerRetryWaitMs` takes the longer of the header wait and the first wait the text names. `markReached` now caps any wait taken from a message or header at `MAX_HINTED_BLOCK_MS` (7 days). The classifier gained `isMetadataOnly`, which decides when the word `terminated` stands alone; reworded variants that carry a reason no longer count as connection failures. I traced the producers and every consumer listed above, plus the new `onSkip` callback in the scheduled-continuation code. In each case the value reaches a branch that uses it.

**Earlier findings, replayed at this head** (probe: `scratch/probe.test.ts`, 2 pass):

- **Astra P1: a hint at the end of the body becomes a near-permanent credential block — closed.**
  - The text `retry-after-ms=200 tail retry-after-ms=86400000` now gives a wait of **200**. Only the hold check reads the longest value (86,400,000), and it can only decline a hold.
  - Text `retry-after-ms=200` with a 9000 ms header wait gives **9000**.
  - `auth-storage-retry-hint-block.test.ts` passes. It covers the echo case, the final-token case, `Number.MAX_VALUE` and the 7-day cap.
- **Claude P3: no upper bound on a credential block — closed** by `MAX_HINTED_BLOCK_MS` in `rotation.ts`.
- **Claude P3: a quoted upstream body ending in a longer hint sets the wait — closed.** The text is now read for its first wait only.
- **Claude P3: an `x-ratelimit-reset` header wait reaches the durable consumers.** This is still intended. The misreading of that header is pre-existing, and the resulting block is now capped at 7 days.
- **Claude P4: "hold ≥ durable" fails by under 1 ms.** This no longer applies: the header wait is now a structured value that feeds `sameModelDelayMs`, so the hold decision sees it directly.
- **Astra P2: extra suffixes stop a wire cut being retried — closed.**
  - `read ECONNRESET after 401 nsec`, `… [fe80::1%eth0]:401` and `… after 403分` all classify as Connection and retriable.
  - So do `after 2 minutes`, `2m30s`, `1.5h`, `request_id=req_503` and ISO timestamps.
- **Astra P2: `terminated` followed by a reason counts as a connection failure — closed.**
  - Three of the four cases now come out as not Connection: `terminated; process killed by SIGKILL`, `terminated (content policy violation)` and `terminated; permission denied`.
  - The fourth, `terminated retry-after-ms=200 due to content policy`, is also not Connection.
  - `terminated`, `terminated.`, `TypeError: terminated`, `terminated (https://h/v1)` and `terminated retry-after-ms=9000` all still classify as Connection.
- **Still open, as the author already disclosed:**
  - Time the provider spends inside one held call.
  - The AggregateError / errors-array, deep status shape, non-English capacity, bare StreamReset and non-Go GOAWAY gaps.
  - All of these fail toward walking the fallback chain.

**Suspicions I ruled out:**
- **`streamSimple` auth-retry rotation loses the header wait.** `createAssistantAuthError` builds an error from the text alone, so `limits.rotate` in `api-key-resolver.ts` and `auth-retry.ts` can't see `errorRetryAfterMs`.
  - If the body states its own wait in the same form and it is shorter than the header's (e.g. `retry-after-ms=200` in the body, `Retry-After: 9` in the header), the first-occurrence reading gives 200.
  - The merge base gives the same 200: its formatter skipped appending whenever `retry-after-ms=` was already in the text. Bodies with no hint, or with a hint in another form, still get the header wait. So this is a pre-existing gap, not something this change introduced.
- **The counter in `withRequestTransport` and `withReplaySafeStreamRetry`.**
  - A fetch that carries a counter but no transport stamp keeps its counter when it re-enters through `transportFetch`, because the counter is inherited.
  - The Vertex token request goes through the uncounted fetch.
  - Undercounting, which would wrongly allow a hold, would need a new counter created partway through a request. I found no path that does this.
- **`socket hang up (400)` classifies as Connection.** The status reader does not take a bare number in parentheses, and that was already true before this change. There is no realistic producer for this text.

**Tests run at this head:**
- `packages/coding-agent`: `auth-storage-retry-hint-block.test.ts` and `agent-session-wire-retry-requests.test.ts`, 36 pass / 0 fail.
- `packages/ai`: my probe, 2 pass.
